This fixture is copied into a separate Go module by
`server.TestExternalAvatarFrontend`, so Go enforces the internal-package import
boundary. The adapter receives only `frontend.Core`; the host fixture supplies
listeners and registers a public plugin. Java775/776 observers use real TCP via
the independent public conformance client. The race build forwards `-race` into
the consumer module.

Coverage is deliberately presence and movement: admission before/after Java,
canonical identity, ordered snapshots/deltas, both directions of movement, existing Java teleport/dimension/mode deltas,
collision correction, plugin veto, attachment teardown, incarnation isolation
and bounded receiver overflow. Privileged commands create the collision fixture
and explicit FIFO observation fences. No inventory, combat, chunk replication,
authentication protocol or complete custom game protocol is claimed.

Numeric Java facts reuse `conformance/testdata/mixed-profile-facts.json` and the
existing official775/776 wire corpus. Negative observations end at explicit
subsequent packets or typed updates, rather than socket-quiet intervals.

Dimension-return movement assertions first wait for fresh avatar spawns: a
Respawn packet alone does not establish the viewer's chunk-backed pairings.
A deliberately unread 775/776 roundtrip also checks that movement committed
before pairing is conveyed by the fresh spawn or a following native movement delta; after that state barrier, the next movement strictly requires a delta.
